ledger.claim: The only contested line is a SGD 3.20 ERP charge for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry at 1.3400, 103.7800. The GPS trace's nearest fix to that point is 7,482.07 m away (nearest fix index 65, 2026-09-21T11:40:50), so no fix comes remotely near the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses to match a gantry to the trace: the vehicle never passed this gantry.

A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). It is refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that correction is available whether or not a deviation exists. The rider is entitled to the whole SGD 3.20 back.

The gantry is flagged on_optimal_route=false on the fare breakdown and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, so this SGD 3.20 was never a properly chargeable ERP or toll pass-through line on either the driven or the optimal route.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd 22.00 and charged_total 25.20. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers any amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines that are properly chargeable; the only excess over the quote is the SGD 3.20 phantom ERP, so the refund is SGD 3.20 in full.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes 'I did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt'. That is an admission about the route and is exactly the kind of independent corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) recognises; the single chat message in evidence is the rider querying the unexpected ERP line, so nothing on the driver's side contests that the gantry was never crossed.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09114-01 carries no payload: no advisory names any road or segment the optimal route traverses, so nothing exonerates the route under POL-RD-03 and the absent advisory is itself citable. There is no closure story behind the extra distance or the ERP line.

The trace records 16.0 km against an optimal 12.5 km - an excess of 3.5 km, or 28%, above both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates of POL-RD-01 - so the deviation itself is established on this trip's own GPS. On an upfront fare the deviation carries no distance or time refund, and the rider does not ask for one; the recovery sought here is the pass-through correction alone.

The rider's initial burden is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-09114 with pickup at 11:22 SGT, satisfying POL-RD-08(a). Rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the 'four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated' trigger for extra corroboration does not apply and no corroboration beyond the trace is required.

Although the ERP line has no counterpart in the trace, POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so this phantom line does not force escalation. The trace is also clean - 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 seconds, 10-second sampling - so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire either and the case can be decided on the money rather than held.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is 22.00, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. However large the measured excess on this route, no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider, and the driver's exposure in this dispute is confined to the pass-through lines on the fare_breakdown.

The rider has carried its initial burden under POL-RD-08 — the trip identifier matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the trace shows an excess of 3.5 km at 28.00% over the booked 12.5 km optimal — but the burden then shifts to the driver, and the driver discharges it by invoking POL-RD-11, the clause that governs this upfront-quoted trip and closes the distance-refund route.

A deviation is established under POL-RD-01, because the trace excess of 3.5 km clears both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates; but at 28.00% and 3.5 km it is far below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality gates, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is therefore not engaged, and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total and no driver-conduct referral can follow from this trip's route.

Even if the POL-RD-06 check were run, the driver's trailing-90-day record is clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, below both the count limb (3 or more) and the ratio limb (0.05 or more with at least 40 trips). No repeat-deviation pattern is established, and no adverse finding may be built on the driver's profile under POL-GEN-01.

The driver cannot invoke POL-RD-03, because the traffic_advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09114-01 carries no payload — no advisory on this record names a road the optimal route traverses, so nothing exonerates the excess; nor POL-RD-04, because the sole chat message is the rider's post-trip fare query, with waypoint_hint null and no road named, so the corroboration test cannot be run; nor POL-RD-05, because neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. None of this costs the driver anything, because under POL-RD-11 the established excess generates no refund on this trip in any event.

The driver does not resist the SGD 3.20 ERP line, and the record does not permit him to. The gantry carries coordinates, and on a trace that is complete and gap-free (coverage_pct 100, no gaps, 10 second sampling) the nearest fix is 7482.07 m away — far outside the 250 m match radius by which POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace — so the line is a billing-integrity failure refundable as a standalone pass-through correction. That correction is the whole of the rider's recovery: it is capped at the 3.20 actually charged, it is not a deviation finding against the driver, and it is not uplifted by any POL-RD-06 limb.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver: I am refunding the SGD 3.20 ERP line and leaving the rest of the fare as charged. The trip was an upfront-quote booking at SGD 22.00. The fare breakdown charged SGD 25.20, made up of the quoted SGD 22.00 plus a SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line. The GPS trace is complete and clean: 100% coverage, 169 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps. Against the gantry coordinates on the fare breakdown (1.3400, 103.7800), the nearest trace fix is 7,482.07 m away at 11:40:50. That is far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses to match a gantry to the trace, so the vehicle did not pass this gantry. The fare breakdown also marks the gantry on_optimal_route=false and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00. The SGD 3.20 is therefore a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): it is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction, not as a distance refund. The Driver's own statement that he did not see or pass the gantry agrees with this. The Rider's recovery is the whole SGD 3.20 contested, so the ruling is FULL_REFUND. On the distance question, the trace shows 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km or 28%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%) but not the materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%). Because the trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 says no distance-or-time refund is available; the rider is already whole on those lines. I have not applied POL-RD-02. The driver-profile check is not required on a non-material deviation, and even if it were run the driver has 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 610 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern and no POL-RD-06(c) referral exists. The traffic advisory artifact carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 does not exonerate; the chat log contains only the rider's post-trip fare query with no waypoint, so POL-RD-04 does not apply; no amendment timestamps or amended optimal distance are present, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The rider's POL-RD-07 corroboration point is not needed because the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). No escalation trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is not impaired, the only unmatched charge is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and there is no contradictory evidence of comparable strength. Confidence is 0.95. The referral below records the billing-integrity finding required by POL-RD-09(4).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — refund the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP charge as an unmatched gantry; the nearest GPS fix is 7,482.07 m from the gantry coordinate, outside the 250 m match radius.
